rationale: Small source-only research product recording a transport-configuration discrepancy: NetworkTransportConfig's InstallSnapshot timeout-scaling comment names a TimeoutScale that the struct does not have, while the constructor always overwrites the transport's own field with the default, so the documented knob is inert. New sources are S64 (the config struct and its comment) and S65 (the constructor override). No map change is proposed, so the accepted map and all accepted results keep their basis; the item is explicitly kept as a lead with its consequence stated and no obligation.

feedback.answered: A further sourced discrepancy was found in the transport configuration surface and recorded as a lead rather than escalated. NetworkTransportConfig documents that 'For InstallSnapshot, we multiply the timeout by (SnapshotSize / TimeoutScale)' (net_transport.go:161-163), but that struct has no TimeoutScale field: the field lives only on the transport itself (net_transport.go:109-110), and NewNetworkTransportWithConfig unconditionally writes DefaultTimeoutScale into it (net_transport.go:226-238), ignoring anything a caller might have expected to configure. So the documented knob for scaling the snapshot send deadline is inert through the public configuration struct, and the only way to change it is to mutate the exported transport field after construction, which the snapshot sender in InstallSnapshot reads directly. The consequence is a tuning gap for slow links or large snapshots rather than a protocol-safety issue, which is why it is recorded as a lead: raising Timeout itself remains an available workaround, though it widens every RPC deadline.
remaining: Whether the ignored knob has ever caused an operational snapshot failure, and whether mutating the exported field is a supported path, are unestablished; the item is a configuration/interface discrepancy with no obligation.
Deployment-level premises of the four confirmed findings are unchanged, as are the ReloadConfig and processHeartbeat leads.
The in-memory snapshot store and observer plumbing remain unread.
